rounds.text: Deep Health AI India Ltd is trading at a compelling valuation of 4.53x P/E and 0.58x price-to-book, severely lagging sector benchmarks of 67.59x and 3.11x respectively [E1, E2, E6, E7]. Fundamental momentum has dramatically outpaced the stock price, evidenced by a 5-year profit growth of 178% compared to a mere 14% share price growth [E19, E23, E55]. The company is virtually debt-free with borrowings reduced to Rs 0.37 Cr and a debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.01x, while concurrently offering an attractive dividend yield of 4.81% [E4, E38, E39, E59]. Furthermore, intrinsic value derived from a discounted cash flow model sits at Rs 4 per share against a market price of Rs 2.08, providing a substantial 43.4% margin of safety [E44, E45]. The reverse DCF implies that today's depressed price of Rs 2.08 requires only 10.0% earnings growth, which is well below the 18.0% base-case assumption [E46]. Sector tailwinds strongly support the setup, with the Consumer Durables sector operating in a tailwind with a score of +0.75 alongside robust sector median metrics [E76, E77, E78, E79]. Conceded: [E34], [E36], [E62], [E64], [E65], [E66].

Deep Health AI India Ltd carries severe fundamental and technical risks that render its low valuation a classic value trap rather than a genuine bargain. The rules-based screen explicitly scores the business a low 32 out of 100 with a sell rating [E66], driven by acute deterioration including a year-over-year net profit collapse of 1202% and a sales contraction of 44% [E71, E72]. Operational efficiency is severely compromised, highlighted by working capital days ballooning from 140 to 405 days alongside dangerously high debtors of 251 days [E65, E64]. This operational strain manifests in deeply negative cash flows, with operating and free cash flows hitting negative Rs 3.64 Cr in March 2026, translating to a terrible cash conversion ratio of -2.80x [E34, E35, E36]. Market confidence is virtually nonexistent, evidenced by a relative-strength rating of 0 against the Nifty 500 [E50], a 12-month price return of -52.9% [E51], and a microscopic promoter holding of just 0.03% [E42]. Conceded: [E44] gives an intrinsic value of Rs 4 per share against a market price of Rs 2.08, and conceded: [E19] shows 178% compounded profit growth over five years.
